translations.translatedText: # Friday 25.5.2018 (radio)

The EU's new data protection regulation has come into force. The Constitutional Law Committee is changing its ways of working because of a data leak. Finnair has ended up on the consumer authority's watch list. Almost 70 percent of cottage owners are from outside the local area.
## The EU data protection regulation came into force
![Reijo Aarnio](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9735210)
Open image viewer
Data Protection Ombudsman Reijo Aarnio. Photo: Matti Hämäläinen / Yle
The EU's new data protection regulation came into force on Friday. Many people have received a lot of mail about it.

The regulation sets out how different organisations must handle personal data. Personal data includes, for example, names, addresses or email addresses. For example, data may only be used for the purposes for which it was originally collected.
Data Protection Ombudsman Reijo Aarnio says that the reform improves the position of an ordinary person.
## A leak in the Constitutional Law Committee
![The Parliament building](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10221818)
Open image viewer
There has been a data leak in Parliament. Photo: Jyrki Lyytikkä / Yle

The Constitutional Law Committee of Parliament is changing its ways of working because of a data leak. From now on the committee will use only paper documents, and it will lock the door outside meeting times. The electronic online workspace will also be shut down.
On Thursday, a draft statement from the Constitutional Law Committee was leaked to several media outlets. The draft concerned the health and social care reform, known as "sote".
Never before has the Constitutional Law Committee had such a wide-ranging leak. The Speaker of Parliament, Paula Risikko, said that Parliament now needs to pull its socks up.
## The Consumer Disputes Board and Finnair
![Passengers at the airport.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-6935330)
Open image viewer
Complaints from air passengers often concern delays. Photo: Elina Ervasti / Yle

The airline Finnair has ended up on the consumer authority's watch list. Companies end up on the Consumer Disputes Board's list if they do not follow the board's recommendations. Finnair is the only state-owned company on the list.

The case that landed Finnair on the list involved the airline not paying a customer a compensation of 600 euros. The compensation concerned a flight delay. The standard compensation amount is based on an EU regulation. Finnair had been on the watch list once before, in 2015.
Last year, Finnair was reported to the authority 700 times.
## Finland has more than half a million cottages
![A summer cottage on a river bank.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9052412)
Open image viewer
Finland has a lot of cottages for a country with a small population. Photo: Pirkko Kukko-Liedes / Yle
Almost 70 percent of cottage owners are from outside the local area.

Statistics Finland's new cottage statistics show that in Kustavi, people from outside the area own more than 90 percent of summer cottages. In Oulu, only about 20 percent of cottages are owned by someone other than a resident of Oulu.

There are about 507,000 cottages in Finland in total. Private individuals own about 430,000 cottages. The most popular cottage municipalities are Kuopio, Mikkeli, Parainen, Lohja and Savonlinna. The top region for cottages is Southwest Finland, with almost 50,000 cottages.

Last year the most new cottages were built in Lapland, South Savo and Southwest Finland. New summer cottages are getting bigger and bigger in floor area. In recent years the average floor area of new cottages has been over 70 square metres.
